item.content:encoded:
My only issue with the article is that I think more could be done with the time-travel aspect; since the serial numbers of past-printed bills match, presumably the serial numbers of future-printed bills will also match. Given the frequency with which redesigns to American currency in particular happen, it seems like the Foundation is in a particularly interesting position to test temporal physics; if we induce or cause a change to currency designs, will the bills change as well? Will the Foundation be unable to do it because the bills we have received from the future look a certain way? Will we cause a CK-class event if we try? Either way, I would think a mention of the temporal implications is in order.

But I upvoted anyway, so I guess you don't have to do shit to please me.

item.title: Re: A downvote - but let me explain
item.content:encoded:
I'll comment on your handful of comments:

- is there any particular reason not to black out the brand of the jeans and the company name?

Because it's not sensitive information by any sense of the word.

- IMHO the year 2018 should also be at least partially blacked out - the article explicitly mentions currency from the future yet unless someone edits the article to update the date or dates from time to time, in just a few years SCP-619 will only produce currency from the past

I'm aware that it'll give dates from the past at some point in the next few years, and I'll make an edit to it around that time. As-is, it is once again not sensitive information.

[issue about dime vs. 10-cent coin]

I considered that, but with US dollars, dime is more concise and unambiguous than "10-cent coin", and more importantly, it makes it easier for (at least US readers) to identify it as "the smallest coin".

As for the other complaints: FaustoV is correct. Further, I deliberately made it more absurd/humorous than it actively needed to be in order to highlight the tragedy of the situation and to provide a sort of whiplash for the reader. That drop between "lol, non-sequential human heads" and "oh god they're killing thousands of sapient beings ACCIDENTALLY" would be smaller, and it would be less enjoyable than a piece played completely straight that tried to insert the same sort of tragedy.

item.title: Re: A downvote - but let me explain
item.content:encoded:
Ok, obviously I'm not the author, but that won't stop me to give you my opinion about your opinion (in an objective way and trying to avoid as much discussion as possible).

First of all, there's actually no problem if a mainlist item gives a sense of humor (specially if it's done right). Most of us thought that the inmobile plastic bag was a direct attempt to troll the Foundation, and I upvoted it (still being a mainlist item). Remember that mainlist items do not neccesarily need to be scary or plain weird as fuck (but at the end this item's new concept has shown a lot of weirdness).

On your different note:

-Censorship is used to avoid unnecesary or dangerous information that people who have contact with the item in question shouldn't know. Here's a brief example:

Dr Shortie: Huh, so it's a Levi. Then why do they blacked-out in the doc if I can see it whenever I handle it?

-If a pair of jeans are spamming dollars from the future, probably people should know about it. Also, remember that in the Foundation, we work with time in a different manner than usual (giving a example with the Xenoplague).

-The last two actually make sense (since I'm a international reader and that confused me a bit, you got a point).

item.title: A downvote - but let me explain
item.content:encoded:
I really like this article, it had me laughing quite loudly in several places. "Non-sequential DNA" still cracks me up! Unfortunately, I do not think it works as a mainlist item. Without the letter, it is a rather bland Horn of Plenty type of thing; with it it feels too ridiculous. So, yeah… Were it a -J I would have happily given it a +1, where it is now it gets the opposite. Pity, really.

On a different note, a handful of comments:
- is there any particular reason not to black out the brand of the jeans and the company name?
- IMHO the year 2018 should also be at least partially blacked out - the article explicitly mentions currency from the future yet unless someone edits the article to update the date or dates from time to time, in just a few years SCP-619 will only produce currency from the past
- what really confuses me is whether the term "dime" should be left as it is or replaced with "a 10-cent coin". On one hand, I think it might be more precise - especially for international readers - to use the latter instead. On the other, while the correspondence between US cents, dimes and dollars is pretty straightforward, trying to do the same with e.g. pre-decimal British pounds would be awkward at best. Besides, "one dime" might sound like a slang term but it is what said coin has actually got *stamped* on it… You can probably see now why I feel confused here, can't you.
